# Safety Committee Guide: Synthetic pump fire, 2024

*Learning purposes: not a statutory document · Learnings drafted by an AI agent from AI-assisted findings*

**Audience:** Joint safety committee and workforce representatives

**Incident:** Synthetic pump fire · 2024-03-20

## Bottom line

- The two top-rated findings sit at supervision and organisational level, not with the crew. [FND-0002; FND-0003]

## What happened

After a seal change, a pump was restarted without a leak test [FND-0001].

## What the investigation says about the system

**Learning:** The job had no checklist to catch a skipped test. [FND-0002]

The procedure index has no return-to-service entry [EVD-0002].

The analysis places the top-rated causes at supervision and organisational level [FND-0002; FND-0003].

## Questions to raise with management

**Q: Who may stop a restart when the test record is missing?** [FND-0001]
- Why it matters: The restart went ahead without one.
- Put to: Maintenance manager

## What to look for on site

- [ ] Is there a leak-test record on the last pump work order? [FND-0001]

## Running the discussion

Ground rules: no names, no blame, talk about conditions.

| Minutes | Item |
|---|---|
| 0-10 | What happened |
| 10-40 | Questions for management |
| 40-60 | Concerns to send on |

## Follow-up

- [ ] Ask to see the new return-to-service checklist. *(30 days)* [FND-0002]
- [ ] Ask for the share of restarts with a test record. *(90 days)* [FND-0001; EVD-0001]
